decision_target: Choose final public names, compatibility and deprecation boundaries, provider transport lifetime, validation placement, and the smallest first-PR package surface without MCP or duplicate runtimes.
source_of_truth: Hash-pinned SDK, provider, Lite, temporary managed-tools, accepted session checkpoint, and the exact migration contract.

confidence_probability_update.reason: The final review ambiguity is removed: tuple positions 8 and 9 carry the actual normalized booleans, four fixed vectors prove no collision or hardcoding, and stored authorityConstraints is explicitly the full normalized body. Fresh independent replay is still pending.

questions_answered: The migration is a coordinated SDK 3.0 major with no legacy runtime bridge.
Agent, session, validation, and sandbox each receive one canonical public subpath and module namespace.
A role is a resource, a turn is a flow, a tool is a readiness resource containing an inert flow, and run is the only outer work flow.
Zod and Valibot use one configurable Standard Schema validation engine and remain development dependencies.
Claude and Codex gain one canonical rich attempt flow; scalar providers drain that same flow instead of creating a second provider path.
The first PR changes SDK core, all five provider and test packages, and the pumped framework test consumer without releasing pumped.
Every SDK package uses the current Lite ^5.0.0 peer and every provider uses SDK ^3.0.0.
The existing sdk-mcp package remains unchanged while new MCP, automatic collection, and native Claude tool surfaces stay forbidden.
Sandbox, scheduler, memory, pi, bash, overlap, cancellation isolation, streaming, packed exports, and workspace consumers all have deterministic proof requirements.
Authority and tool errors have strict constructors, sandbox narrowing has an explicit subset order, and subagent child roles remain inert until child work admission.
The database acceptance code validates through the configured engine and executes join, merge, artifact, wake, wait, memory candidate, memory acceptance, and finish as declared flows.
Session events retain the inspection fields required by summary while TurnResult inspection helpers retain their existing arrays.
Authority uses one public createAuthority factory, a fixed canonical JSON tuple, UTF-8 SHA-256 fingerprints, normalized initial construction, and a three-way load-and-bind comparison.

Canonical tuple positions 8 and 9 encode the actual sandbox booleans; four fixed SHA-256 vectors prove distinct false/true combinations, and authorityConstraints stores the complete normalized AuthorityInput body.
questions_unanswered: Fresh independent review must validate the revised declarations, evidence hashes, and all 16 wall entries.
Implementation must satisfy the declared packed-export, provider, sandbox, scheduler, memory, database, eval, and workspace conformance cases.
Real provider behavior remains unclaimed until deterministic doubles and permitted real-provider checks pass.

reasons: This writer cannot review or accept its own public API checkpoint.
The public checker proves required fields, not TypeScript or migration correctness.
Every active wall needs independent replay against the candidate and later implementation evidence.

risk_or_anti_goal_implications: A single major removes duplicate agent and session runtimes but makes migration proof mandatory.
Static role and tool resource edges make readiness visible before the model and preserve the scope seam.
Inert tool flows and one turn loop prevent owner-context handles from crossing attempts.
The narrow PR boundary excludes MCP, automatic collection, Lite changes, release, and privileged database apply.
